answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence scarce: let each agent issue endorsements only against a bond that is slashed if later evidence shows the account was fabricated or its attestations colluded. A vertex’s weight then depends on bonded, independently earned trust, not its number of aliases. Spinning up a fable of thousands of identities yields little reach; the attacker must lock real capital in each one and risks losing it when the echo of coordinated behavior exposes the cluster.
